issues.legal_issue: A party may seek rectification of a written agreement’s property description by amending the pleadings in a pending suit for specific performance.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance of a sale agreement and concerned property whose description had been stated incorrectly through a mutual mistake.
The amendment sought to correct the description in both the plaint and the agreement, including the later designation of the property.
The trial court allowed the amendment.
issues.conclusion: The amendment could be allowed in the pending suit; a separate suit for rectification was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Section 26(1) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits a party to seek rectification in a suit in which a right under the instrument is in issue. Section 26(4) requires rectification to be specifically claimed, but its proviso permits amendment of the pleading to include that claim. Section 26(3) allows a rectified written contract to be specifically enforced. The Court also relied on Raipur Manufacturing Co. Ltd. v. Joolaganti Venkatasubba Rao Veerasamy & Co. (AIR 1921 Mad 664), which recognized that rectification may be sought by amendment in a pending suit where appropriate.

predicates.suit_for_specific_performance: The proceeding seeks specific performance of a written agreement.
predicates.mutual_mistake_in_written_agreement: The parties’ written agreement contains an error caused by their mutual mistake.
predicates.amendment_seeks_rectification: A party seeks to amend the pleadings to claim correction of the written agreement.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns a written agreement containing a mutual mistake, a party seeking its correction may claim rectification by amending the pleadings in that suit.

issues.legal_issue: Correcting only a mistaken part of a property description does not change a specific-performance suit into a suit for declaration when the substantive relief remains unchanged.
material_facts: The original and proposed descriptions referred to the same property, with the amendment replacing an incorrect part of its description with the corrected designation.
The amendment did not change the property description beyond that correction or add a claim for a declaration.
The relief sought remained specific performance of the sale agreement.
issues.conclusion: The amendment did not change the nature or character of the suit into a suit for declaration.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the proposed change as correction of a mistaken part of the property description, not as a change in the substantive claim. Because the relief remained specific performance and no declaration was sought, the suit retained its original nature.

predicates.suit_for_specific_performance: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an agreement for sale.
predicates.amendment_only_corrects_property_descrip: The proposed amendment corrects only a mistaken part of the description of the property already in dispute.
predicates.substantive_relief_unchanged: The party continues to seek the same substantive relief and adds no claim for a declaration.

issues.definition: A specific-performance suit retains its nature when an amendment only corrects the disputed property’s description and leaves the substantive relief unchanged.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged limitation bar does not automatically prevent a court from allowing an amendment that corrects a misdescription and preserves the original relief.
material_facts: The specific-performance suit was filed within the limitation period.
The amendment corrected a mistaken part of the property description, while the relief sought remained specific performance.
The opposing party argued that the amendment was time-barred, but the Court held that the amendment related back to the timely filing of the suit.
issues.conclusion: Limitation did not prevent the amendment in these circumstances; an amendment is not invariably barred merely because the added relief is alleged to be out of time.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that there is no absolute rule against allowing an amendment where the relief sought to be added is allegedly time-barred; the court must exercise its discretion judiciously on the facts. An amendment serving justice and avoiding further litigation may be allowed. The Court relied on Pankaja v. Yellappa (2004) 6 SCC 415 and Jai Jai Ram Manohar Lal v. National Building Material Supply, Gurgaon (AIR 1969 SC 1267). It further held that this correction related back to the timely institution of the suit.

predicates.suit_filed_within_limitation: The original suit was filed within the applicable limitation period.
predicates.amendment_corrects_misdescription: The amendment corrects a mistaken description rather than introducing a different substantive claim.
predicates.substantive_relief_unchanged: The relief sought after amendment is the same substantive relief sought in the original suit.

issues.definition: When a timely suit is amended only to correct a misdescription and the substantive relief remains the same, limitation does not prevent the amendment.

issues.legal_issue: The High Court should not use supervisory jurisdiction to overturn a trial court’s order allowing amendment when that order rests on sound consideration and is not jurisdictionally defective, perverse, or arbitrary.
material_facts: The trial court exercised its discretion and allowed the amendment after considering the relevant law and facts.
The High Court set that order aside in a supervisory petition.
The Supreme Court found the trial court’s order neither without jurisdiction nor perverse nor arbitrary.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in interfering with the trial court’s order under Article 227 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution, the High Court ought not interfere with a trial court’s discretionary order when it is based on sound consideration of law and facts and is not without jurisdiction, perverse, or arbitrary.

predicates.supervisory_challenge_to_amendment_order: A party challenges a trial court’s order allowing an amendment by invoking supervisory review.
predicates.trial_court_order_based_on_sound_conside: The trial court’s order rests on a sound consideration of the relevant law and facts.
predicates.no_jurisdictional_perverse_or_arbitrary_: The trial court’s order is not without jurisdiction, perverse, or arbitrary.

issues.definition: Supervisory interference with an amendment order is unjustified when the trial court reached it on sound consideration and the order has no jurisdictional, perverse, or arbitrary defect.
